invariant: After SvekResult's LimitFinder pass, PlantUML translates a cluster RectangleArea by adding the same normalization delta independently to min and max. Final symbol dimensions are then recomputed as translated max minus translated min. IEEE-754 cancellation can move an exact integer dimension one ULP below that integer even though its formatted geometry is unchanged. USymbolCloud casts those final dimensions to long when deriving its deterministic random seed.
causal_divergence: Rust translated ClusterPosition.x and y during SVEK envelope normalization but retained the pre-translation width and height fields. In the valid filled packageStyle cloud counterexample, both measurement paths see 171.0 by 99.00000000000001. PlantUML's final translated RectangleArea becomes 170.99999999999997 by 99.00000000000001, selecting width seed 170. A JDK debugger at USymbolCloud.drawCloud observed both Java calls directly, and reflective invocation of the JAR's private frontier method reproduced the expected and actual first curves for those two adjacent widths. The endpoint operation must occur after the final render-margin translation. It also depends on Java-exact cloud distance arithmetic: Rust's hypot-based measurement origin makes the derived width 171.00000000000003, so endpoint recomputation alone does not change the integer seed.
planned_change: At LayoutPackageCluster construction, after the final render-margin translation, reconstruct width and height by adding each extent to the translated minimum and subtracting that same minimum, exactly as RectangleArea.move followed by getWidth/getHeight does. Do not round or special-case clouds; the endpoint arithmetic belongs to the shared cluster model. Combine this with Java-exact cloud CoordinateChange distance arithmetic so the translated origin itself matches.
